subject: Logic
title: What Makes an Argument Fallacious
description: Learn What Makes an Argument Fallacious in one minute.

hook.text: An argument can sound brilliant and still be broken. The flaw hides in the reasoning, not the words.

buildup.text: A fallacy is an error in reasoning that makes an argument invalid—even if the conclusion happens to be true.

discovery.text: "She's nice, so she must be honest." The conclusion might be right, but niceness doesn't prove honesty.

twist.text: Fallacies aren't lies. The person using one may genuinely believe their argument is sound.

climax.text: Learning fallacies lets you spot broken reasoning—in others and, more importantly, in yourself.

punchline.text: Convincing and correct aren't the same.
